terms.comment: A length goes in the accusative: septem pedēs longus, seven feet long (Plin. NH 6.212, Lewis & Short). Of a person, longus is a colloquial “lanky” (Catull. 67.47, Lewis & Short). For a long time, see long (for a long time).

phrases.latin: ratem ūnam ducentōs longam pedēs, quīnquāgintā lātam ā terrā in amnem porrēxērunt
phrases.english: they ran a raft two hundred feet long and fifty wide out from the bank into the river

phrases.latin: omnia ista in longā vītā sunt, quōmodo in longā viā et pulvis et lutum et pluvia
phrases.english: all that comes with a long life, as dust, mud and rain come with a long road

phrases.latin: quīndecim mīlia passuum in longitūdinem patēns
Vōcālis est longa nātūrā aut positiōne.
phrases.english: A vowel is long by nature or by position.
